title: 409. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Sine Cosine and Tangent in Right Triangles
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: State the sine of an acute angle of a right triangle as a ratio of sides.
questions.question: In a right triangle, \(\theta\) is one of the acute angles. Which ratio defines \(\sin\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The sine of an acute angle is the length of the side opposite the angle divided by the length of the hypotenuse. The ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse is the cosine of the angle.
questions.hint: Recall which side is used for sine and which for cosine; both ratios have the hypotenuse as denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the cosine of an acute angle from the three side lengths of a right triangle.
questions.question: A right triangle has legs \(3\) and \(4\) and hypotenuse \(5\). The angle \(\theta\) is opposite the leg of length \(3\). What is \(\cos\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The leg of length \(3\) is opposite \(\theta\), so the leg of length \(4\) is adjacent to \(\theta\). Hence \(\cos\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{4}{5}\). The ratio \(\frac{3}{5}\) is \(\sin\theta\).
questions.hint: Decide which leg touches the angle; that leg is the adjacent side.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the tangent of an acute angle from the two legs of a right triangle.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite an acute angle \(\theta\) has length \(5\) and the side adjacent to \(\theta\) has length \(12\). What is \(\tan\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The tangent is the opposite side divided by the adjacent side: \(\tan\theta=\frac{5}{12}\). The reciprocal \(\frac{12}{5}\) is the tangent of the other acute angle.
questions.hint: Tangent compares the two legs; put the side opposite the angle in the numerator.

questions.learningObjective: Use the Pythagorean theorem to find the hypotenuse and then a sine ratio.
questions.question: A right triangle has legs of lengths \(8\) and \(15\). What is the sine of the angle opposite the leg of length \(8\)?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=\sqrt{289}=17\). The sine is the opposite side over the hypotenuse, \(\frac{8}{17}\). The ratio \(\frac{8}{15}\) compares the two legs and is the tangent of that angle.
questions.hint: Sine needs the hypotenuse; find it with the Pythagorean theorem first.

questions.concept: Cofunction relation in a right triangle
questions.learningObjective: Relate the sine of one acute angle to the cosine of the other acute angle.
questions.question: In triangle \(ABC\) the angle at \(C\) is \(90^\circ\) and \(\sin A=\frac{3}{5}\). What is \(\cos B\)?
questions.explanation: The side opposite \(A\) is the side adjacent to \(B\), and both ratios use the same hypotenuse. Therefore \(\cos B=\sin A=\frac{3}{5}\). The value \(\frac{4}{5}\) is \(\cos A\), which equals \(\sin B\).
questions.hint: Label the side opposite \(A\) and ask what role it plays for angle \(B\).

questions.learningObjective: Find another trigonometric ratio of an acute angle from a given ratio.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\) of a right triangle, \(\sin\theta=\frac{5}{13}\). What is \(\tan\theta\)?
questions.explanation: Take the opposite side as \(5\) and the hypotenuse as \(13\). The adjacent side is \(\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=\sqrt{144}=12\). Then \(\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{5}{12}\). The ratio \(\frac{12}{13}\) is \(\cos\theta\).
questions.hint: Draw a right triangle with opposite side \(5\) and hypotenuse \(13\), and find the missing leg.

questions.learningObjective: Use the side ratios of a special right triangle to evaluate a tangent.
questions.question: A right triangle has angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\), with the shorter leg of length \(1\), the longer leg of length \(\sqrt{3}\), and hypotenuse \(2\). What is \(\tan 60^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The larger acute angle, \(60^\circ\), is opposite the longer leg \(\sqrt{3}\) and adjacent to the shorter leg \(1\). Hence \(\tan 60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1}=\sqrt{3}\). The value \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) is \(\tan 30^\circ\).
questions.hint: The larger acute angle is opposite the longer leg.

questions.concept: Possible values of sine and tangent
questions.learningObjective: Decide which values a trigonometric ratio of an acute angle can take.
questions.question: Which statement is impossible for an acute angle \(\theta\) of a right triangle?
questions.explanation: The sine is a leg divided by the hypotenuse, and the hypotenuse is the longest side, so \(0<\sin\theta<1\). Thus \(\sin\theta=\frac{5}{4}\) is impossible. The tangent compares the two legs, and a triangle with legs \(5\) and \(4\) gives \(\tan\theta=\frac{5}{4}\), so that value is possible.
questions.hint: Compare the length of a leg with the length of the hypotenuse.

questions.concept: Sine in an isosceles right triangle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sine ratio in an isosceles right triangle with given legs.
questions.question: An isosceles right triangle has two legs of length \(7\). What is the sine of one of its acute angles?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{7^2+7^2}=7\sqrt{2}\). The sine of an acute angle is \(\frac{7}{7\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). The value \(\frac{1}{2}\) would require the hypotenuse to be \(14\), twice a leg, which is not the case here.
questions.hint: Find the hypotenuse with the Pythagorean theorem, then rationalise the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Construct a right triangle from a tangent value to find the sine of the same angle.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\) of a right triangle, \(\tan\theta=2\). What is \(\sin\theta\)?
questions.explanation: Take the opposite side as \(2\) and the adjacent side as \(1\). The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt{5}\). Then \(\sin\theta=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}\). The value \(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\) is \(\cos\theta\).
questions.hint: Choose convenient leg lengths whose ratio is \(2\), then find the hypotenuse.
